verdict.justification: Both deliverables use the quoted inputs, the 70:30 mix, Year-1 tooling recovery and equally split upfront R&D, and both reach the same reasonable recommendation of Vendocrat. A is more useful for the nomination review because it adds side-by-side variant NPVs and a more targeted sensitivity to Solimoto’s ambiguous quantity threshold: “ANNUAL headlamp quantity per variant” rather than only B’s lower-price-from-Year-1 scenario. A also provides stronger closing conditions, including Year-4 capacity confirmation, firm lifecycle prices and tooling ownership, and explains why allocated variant NPVs cannot simply support a split award. B is more concise and includes useful tooling and R&D reconciliation checks, but its assumptions sheet contains an apparent invalid formula in a source-note cell, “formula= 1 - top share”. A needs a small editorial correction: its claimed percentage savings use Vendocrat’s cost as the denominator, so they are competitor premiums rather than percentages below the competitors’ costs. Overall, A’s fuller treatment of quotation ambiguity and nomination conditions narrowly outweighs B’s cleaner presentation.
